findings.title: Facebook README tells operators a connect_failed park ends only with docker stop (a new container = a Facebook login); 0.15.0 added Mark healthy / resume and timeout retries
findings.evidence: README: timeouts 'raise ConnectFailedError at once' and 'Only `docker stop` ends it (exit 0)'. trackers/facebook/CHANGELOG.md 0.15.0 (RS-454): a timeout is retried twice more (10 s, 30 s) and a connect_failed park accepts the ERP's one-shot resume directive (Mark healthy, ERP v1.380.0); backend apps/backend/src/fleet/claim.ts:494-533 hands out resume. FEATURES.md 3690-3700 documents Mark healthy.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator with a worker parked on 'Page didn't load' follows the README and docker-stops it; the replacement container restores the session, i.e. a Facebook login the AGENTS.md first rule forbids, when Mark healthy would have resumed in the same browser.
findings.proposed_fix: At :496 replace 'Only `docker stop` ends it (exit 0).' with: '**Mark healthy** on the ERP Fleet page sends a one-shot `resume` heartbeat directive for a `connect_failed` park: the worker clears its parked state and asks for a task again in the same browser, with no login (0.15.0). `login_failed`, `browser_failed` and `crashed` parks ignore it. `docker stop` (exit 0) means a new container, which is a Facebook login.' Replace the timeout clause at ~:484 with: 'a timeout is tried twice more in the same page, 10 s and 30 s apart (0.15.0), before it raises ConnectFailedError'. At :465-468 change "an operator's `relogin` directive" to "an operator's `relogin` or, for `connect_failed`, `resume` directive".
findings.regression_test: none (docs); optional grep check in CI

findings.title: Facebook README says to restart workers after editing search settings, contradicting the repo's first rule
findings.evidence: README: 'After editing, regenerate worker configs with `rsc gen-configs` and restart the workers.' AGENTS.md 'First rule': never restart a worker to pick up a setting; every restart is a login. configs/generated/ does not exist in trackers/facebook/configs (only homelab.toml template remains), and ERP fleet workers take settings from their claim.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator tuning search_interval follows the README and restarts the fleet: every worker logs in again, risking checkpoints (26 of 41 accounts were already parked on 2026-10-24).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace :1208-1209 with: 'ERP fleet workers read search settings from their claim and the Fleet Rules dialog; a change reaches each worker at its next task. Never restart a worker to pick up a setting: a restart is a Facebook login (see AGENTS.md).'

findings.evidence: Only configs/homelab.toml (template) remains; deploy/docker-compose.homelab*.yml are gone (ls trackers/facebook/deploy), so scripts/deploy.sh homelab_workers() (:78-85) yields nothing and it rebuilds coordinator+console only (:311,:367-371). trackers/facebook/CHANGELOG 0.14.8-0.14.14 retired/handed over every legacy launch. At the top of :339 add: 'Superseded for ERP fleet workers by apps/fleet-agent. rs_fleetd applies only where rs-fleetd still runs; every worker a release recreates is a Facebook login.' Replace the :251-300 step list with 'test, rebuild coordinator + console, verify; deploy.sh no longer touches workers (none are in compose) and ERP fleet workers are released from the ERP.'
